subject.title: Unhandled Playwright assertion error in CRSession._onMessage crashes Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw handle this crash class with a narrow Playwright assertion classifier, browser-profile quarantine/reconnect, or a larger browser/CDP subprocess isolation design?
rationale: The source path is clear enough to keep this open, but the durable fix depends on how much unknown Playwright state OpenClaw should suppress in the main Gateway process and how browser failures should affect unrelated sessions.

options.title: Design browser recovery boundary first
options.body: Keep this issue open and have a browser/Gateway owner specify recovery semantics, live proof requirements, and the boundary between fatal process errors and isolated browser-profile failures.

options.title: Accept a narrow classifier
options.body: Treat only well-identified Playwright CDP assertion shapes as non-fatal while leaving unknown unhandled rejections fatal.

options.title: Wait for live repro before implementation
options.body: Require a fresh current-main CRSession CDP reproduction before choosing any code path, preserving this report as production context.

recommendation.title: Design browser recovery boundary first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and have a browser/Gateway owner specify recovery semantics, live proof requirements, and the boundary between fatal process errors and isolated browser-profile failures.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main history across the unhandled-rejection handler and browser CDP ownership boundary.
